summary: The Indian threat picture this month is pulled in two directions at once: high-volume, financially-motivated mobile fraud hitting citizens at scale, and patient, state-aligned intrusion aimed at government, defence and critical infrastructure. The common seam is the edge — VPNs, firewalls and cloud identity — which is where ransomware crews and espionage actors alike still get their first foothold.

items.title: Fake-APK UPI fraud has gone industrial
items.why: This is no longer lone scammers. Organised mule networks are running fake RTO / e-challan APKs end to end — a single Mumbai bust traced roughly ₹43 crore, with parallel networks in Pune and Ahmedabad. The money moves through first-time payees and mule fan-out faster than most risk controls react, and the malware (GhostBat RAT and kin) reads the OTP and captures the UPI PIN on-device. For any payments operator, this is the live, high-volume threat — not a future one.

items.title: The edge is still the way in
items.why: The India-relevant watchlist is dominated by internet-facing edge: Ivanti Connect Secure, Citrix NetScaler, PAN-OS, Fortinet, plus SharePoint (CVE-2025-53770, EPSS ~100%, ransomware-linked). These are precisely the products Indian enterprises expose to the internet and precisely the ones ransomware crews mass-exploit within days of a PoC. If you do one thing this month, make it edge patch cadence — it is the single highest-leverage control on this list.

items.title: Pakistan-nexus espionage is persistent, not episodic
items.why: Transparent Tribe (APT36) and SideCopy continue to target Indian government, defence, education and research with Crimson RAT and the ZIP→LNK→LOLBin delivery pattern. These are not one-off campaigns; they are a standing collection effort that re-tools faster than it disappears. If you sit in gov, defence or academia, assume you are in scope and detect for the delivery chain, not just the final implant.

items.title: Identity is the new perimeter — watch M365 sign-ins
items.why: FrostArmada (APT28) demonstrated adversary-in-the-middle token theft fronting Outlook on the web via SOHO-router DNS hijack. As Indian orgs move onto M365 / Entra, a high-risk sign-in that survives MFA is worth more to an attacker than any single endpoint. The signals to wire up now are Entra sign-in risk and unexpected endpoint DNS changes — together they catch this chain.

items.title: China-nexus pre-positioning in the power sector
items.why: RedEcho's targeting of load dispatch centres is about access held for later, not immediate disruption — lower tempo, higher stakes. This is the kind of intrusion that matters in a crisis rather than a quarterly report, and it belongs on the radar of anyone defending Indian critical infrastructure even when nothing is visibly happening.
